_doc: Kesh, the Breachwarden (the Chainward). Keeps the hellgate in Basecamp Hell. Pool 'kesh'. Model: CharacterRoster npc 'breachwarden'.

lines.text: Halt. Name, sin, and reason for ascending.
{demon}. All of them. Because I was told to.
Correct answers. Kesh, of the Chainward. I keep the Breach. Nothing goes up without my halberd hitting the floor, and nothing comes down that I did not count.
You will come down. They all do. I will count you.
Warden Skarn. The Chainward salutes you.
At ease, Kesh. The deepest pit misses you.
The deepest pit misses nobody, Warden. That is why it works.
Three times down. I have notched it on the halberd.
Do not take it personally. I notch everything. The haft is mostly notches now.
The Breach is wider than when we tore it. A hand's width every week.
Either the Verge is giving way, or something on the other side is pulling. I do not like either answer.
We took an angel alive last week. Chained it in the low cells.
It did not beg. It did not curse. It just kept asking the wall whether anyone was listening.
I have kept prisoners for nine hundred years, Sinbound. That is the first one I pitied.
Ossek tells me the road goes all the way up now. To the Seventh Gate.
When you are ready, I will open the Breach wider than it has ever been opened. All of it. Every chain off.
Take the road to Heaven's Gate. Break the wards, fell the warden, and walk through. The Gate opens for those who know about the March. You do.
Up, then. I will be here to count you down.
Stand clear of the Breach. It bites the careless.
Every chain holds something. Remember what you hold.
Counted. Again.
Seraph. You fell through here once. I counted you then, too.
Hexbinder. Do not write in my count.
Warden. The Breach holds. As you ordered.
Ravager. Please do not headbutt the gate on your way out. Again.
Reaper. You are the only one who comes back as quietly as you leave.
Hive. I count you as one. The Chainward has agreed not to argue about it.
Hive. The Breach counts a soul for every demon that goes up. When you go up, the count goes strange.
One soul. Then a thousand. Then one again. I have stopped trying to make it add up.
Neither do we.
Gatekeeper. One keeper of doors to another: you broke the only rule there is. I respect it more than I should.
Gatekeeper. You held the First Gate. I hold the Breach. Tell me, honestly: what does it feel like to open a door you swore to keep shut?
Like breathing out, after holding it for an age.
...I will not open the Breach without orders. But I will think about that answer for a long time.
